channel.title: Hastings Daily
channel.description: Local news for Hastings, St Leonards, Rye, Bexhill and Battle, three times a day.

item.title: Hastings council to consider Age Friendly strategy for older residents
item.description: Hastings Borough Council has drawn up an Age Friendly Hastings Strategy and Action Plan, with proposals to make the town more accessible and inclusive for people aged 50 and over.

item.title: Ark Alexandra CCF wins three honours at Lord-Lieutenant's Awards
item.description: Ark Alexandra Academy's Combined Cadet Force had a triple win at the Lord-Lieutenant's Awards Ceremony, held at Lancing College and attended by senior military personnel and civic representatives from across the region.

item.title: Police increase patrols in Eldridge Way area of St Leonards
item.description: Police said they are increasing patrols in and around Eldridge Way, St Leonards, near The Ridge, following reports of anti-social behaviour from local residents.

item.title: Rye station to close from 3pm for bonfire celebrations
item.description: Southern has announced that Rye railway station will be closed from 3pm on the day of the town's bonfire celebrations, Saturday, 14 November, until the regular start of service the next day, Sunday.

item.title: Former St Leonards church becomes community hub with weekly market
item.description: A former church in St Leonards has become a thriving community hub, hosting a popular weekly market and serving as a venue for concerts and events.

item.title: Update: Developers reveal bid to build 120 new Hastings homes
item.description: Catesby Estates and Rurban Estates are now inviting people to have a say on the proposals before finalising them and submitting planning applications to Hastings Borough Council and Rother District Council. The development would include approximately 120 new homes, of which 30 per cent would be affordable housing, a care home, a new landscaped public open green space and children's play area. Many readers have voiced concerns about traffic on The Ridge and pressure on local services, according to the Hastings Observer. Feedback can be shared via a consultation at www.catesby-hastings.co.uk.

item.title: Free parking at Hastings council car parks in December
item.description: Hastings Borough Council has agreed plans to provide free parking at its council-owned car parks on specific dates in the run-up to Christmas.

item.title: Bexhill councillor calls parking permit charges 'extortionate'
item.description: A Bexhill town councillor has branded the price of residential parking permits in the town 'extortionate and over the top'.

item.title: Toilets top of residents' list in £21.5m Pride in Place survey
item.description: New toilets have topped the list of improvements residents want in Hastings, after MP Helena Dollimore asked how the £21.5 million of Government Pride in Place funding should be spent.

item.title: One East Sussex reorganisation to proceed, with four Lewes wards moving to Brighton
item.description: The Government has announced it is minded to proceed with local government reorganisation in East Sussex, Hastings Borough Council has said.

item.title: Charity raises £4,000 to save Bexhill Hospital stroke rehabilitation service
item.description: Becky, Sarah and Owen from the #DoItForJosh charity met the team at Bexhill Hospital’s Irvine Unit on Monday to mark the continuation of a vital local stroke rehabilitation programme.

item.title: Cooden Beach Golf Club seeks permission for homes on part of its course
item.description: Cooden Beach Golf Club is seeking planning permission to build housing on part of its course on Cooden Sea Road, according to an application to Rother District Council.

item.title: Westfield says farewell to Christmas Lights co-founder Ken Munday BEM
item.description: Westfield, outside Hastings, has paid its respects to Ken Munday, who was awarded the British Empire Medal for his services to the village.

item.title: On this day, 1896: This week in 1896: first moving pictures shown on St Leonards Pier
item.description: This week in 1896, the first moving pictures to be shown in Hastings and St Leonards were seen on St Leonards Pier, the local record shows.

item.title: Man convicted of 18 offences after shop thefts in Hastings
item.description: Tom Marchant, 44, of no fixed address, has been convicted of 18 offences after a series of shop thefts in Hastings, Sussex Police have reported.

item.title: Bird deaths spark campaign to remove netting in Hastings and Rother
item.description: A new local campaign is calling for safer ways to manage birds around buildings after three incidents in which birds became trapped in netting.

item.title: Residents brand St Leonards metal supports an 'eyesore'
item.description: Residents have branded large metal supports in St Leonards an 'eyesore'.

item.title: Developers reveal bid to build 120 new Hastings homes
item.description: Catesby Estates and Rurban Estates have revealed a bid to build about 120 new homes in Hastings.

item.title: Battle Bonfire returns to the Abbey Green on Saturday
item.description: Battle holds what is said to be the oldest Guy Fawkes bonfire celebrations in England on Saturday 7 November, with the town's tradition tracing back to 1646. St Mary's Church then allocated two shillings and sixpence for gunpowder treason rejoicing, and the Battel Bonfire Boyes have kept the custom alive ever since.

item.title: Bexhill care home wins Pet Friendly Care Home Award
item.description: Elizabeth Court Rest Home in Hastings Road, Bexhill, has won the Pet Friendly Care Home Award for 2026. The home, which provides residential care for older people, lets its residents bring their own pets with them when they move in.

item.title: Free off-grid solar workshops coming to Hastings and Battle
item.description: Energise Sussex Coast, a local community benefit society, is holding free workshops on off-grid solar power in Hastings and Battle this month. The sessions are aimed at anyone who wants to build a small, fully off-grid solar system for a shed, workshop, van or truck, and no technical background is needed.

item.title: Eight Hastings and Bexhill residents arrested outside US embassy
item.description: Eight residents of Hastings and Bexhill were arrested outside the US embassy in London on Saturday 31 October, the Hastings Online Times reported. The group was peacefully holding signs reading 'I oppose genocide. I support Palestine Action'.

item.title: Coalition says October's budget cut the Warm Homes Plan by up to £5.7bn
item.description: A fuel poverty coalition says the government's October budget failed to protect households on the coast from volatile gas prices, and cut the Warm Homes Plan by up to £5.7 billion.

item.title: Martin Cohen to launch new book at Hastings Palestine Solidarity event
item.description: Bestselling philosophy writer Martin Cohen is returning to Hastings to launch his latest book on Wednesday 11 November.

item.title: Hastings joins in the 'Dusking' morris-dancing tradition
item.description: A new autumn ritual called 'Dusking' has reached the Hastings seafront, bringing morris dancing to the town's darkening days.

item.title: On this day, 1940: An air raid damages every house on The Lawn, St Leonards
item.description: On 11 November 1940, an air attack reached The Lawn, a road of semi-detached houses in St Leonards.

item.title: Police appeal to find Orion, 15, last seen in St Leonards
item.description: Police are appealing to the public to help find a missing 15-year-old boy who was last seen in St Leonards on Saturday (31 October).

item.title: On this day, 1597: A storm swept away the old Hastings harbour
item.description: A storm swept away the town's harbour on this day in 1597. Between 1595 and 1597, a large and expensive harbour, known as the 'pier', was built in front of Hastings Old Town. On 1 November 1597, a storm swept it away.

item.title: Secondary school applications close at midnight today
item.description: Parents and carers in East Sussex have until midnight today to submit applications for secondary school places for September 2027.

item.title: Beachy Head naval battle book published posthumously
item.description: The final book from late Shoreham-based lawyer Quintin Barry, Beachy Head 1690: The Grand Alliance at Bay, has been published after his death in January 2025, aged 88.

item.title: Christmas Makers' Fair at De La Warr Pavilion on 7 November
item.description: Bexhill Artists' Workspace is holding its Christmas Makers' Fair at The Studio, De La Warr Pavilion, Bexhill, on Saturday 7 November.

item.title: Iden's The Bell pub moves closer to reopening after plans submitted
item.description: A village pub that has been closed for years could reopen with three new guest rooms, after renovation plans were submitted to Rother District Council.

item.title: Status Quo's Francis Rossi to play De La Warr Pavilion, Bexhill
item.description: Francis Rossi is to bring his solo Status Quo show to Bexhill this month. The guitarist will perform his Songbook: Quo – Past, Present, Future tour at the De La Warr Pavilion on Tuesday, November 10, the Sussex Express reports.

item.title: Local author Elizabeth Webb's new novel reviewed
item.description: A new book by locally based author Elizabeth Webb has been reviewed by Michael Salmon in the Hastings Online Times. Dexter's Lot, published by BiblioMuso, follows its protagonist as he stumbles "from the exciting world of rock music to the mundane world of the supermarket," enduring many trials along the way.

item.title: On this day, 2006: The last traders left Hastings Pier
item.description: On 31 October 2006, the last traders on Hastings Pier left the boardwalks. The National Piers Society's news archive records that the businesses on the Promenade Extension, which had remained open, left on that day, and the final event was a Hallowe'en party in the Gritti Palace pub. By the end of it, the structure was padlocked and deserted.

item.title: Hastings Cabinet to discuss fee freeze and heritage funding on 9 November
item.description: Hastings Borough Council's Cabinet will meet on Monday 9 November to discuss a range of reports, the council said.

item.title: Update: Eastbourne MP calls for shuttle bus between Eastbourne and Hastings hospitals
item.description: The call for a shuttle bus between Eastbourne District General Hospital and the Conquest Hospital in Hastings has sparked widespread debate on The Herald's Facebook page, according to the paper. Many people commented in favour of the suggestion, while others asked practical questions, including what happens when a bus is full or whether people would need to book. Some readers said the focus should instead be on restoring all of Eastbourne DGH's services.

item.title: Dee Day White retires after 34 years running yard in Courthouse Street
item.description: Dee Day White is retiring after running a popular antique and bric-a-brac mews and yard in Courthouse Street, Hastings Old Town, for the past 34 years.

item.title: New police policy will see illegal e-bikes and e-scooters seized from Sunday
item.description: Sussex Police and Surrey Police have introduced a tougher policy under which riders caught using illegal electric vehicles in public could have their vehicles seized and destroyed.

item.title: Update: Bexhill empty shops plan opens for public consultation
item.description: The council leader says the draft Local Plan consultation remains open until Tuesday, November 24, and the Tapestry development in Battle, which will provide 200 energy-efficient homes, has been shortlisted for the Best Development Award at the Inside Housing Development Awards.

item.title: Update: Holiday lets, flats and shops approved for arcade blaze site in George Street
item.description: Residents have divided over the approved scheme. One, writing on the Observer's Facebook page, said: "We don't need holiday lets and more shops; we need housing." Others suggested affordable bedsits or a hub for young people, while a handful backed the development.

item.title: St Michael's Hospice opens Festive Market in St Leonards
item.description: St Michael's Hospice is holding a two-day Festive Market at its Upper Maze Hill site in St Leonards on Saturday, November 14, and Sunday, November 15.

item.title: Ocean Symposium returns to Bexhill in November
item.description: Bexhill is to host an Ocean Symposium and Marine Exhibition at St Peter's Community Centre on Saturday, November 14.

item.title: Update: Bexhill seafront fountain replacement reaches procurement stage
item.description: More has emerged on the plans to reinstate the fountain on the front lawns of the De La Warr Pavilion in Bexhill. Rother District Council will lead the procurement process as both landowner and accountable body for the funding, and Bexhill-on-Sea Town Council has agreed in principle to take on future maintenance responsibilities, subject to lease and construction quality arrangements, The Argus reported. The project forms part of the Bexhill Neighbourhood Board's four-year Regeneration Investment Plan and is funded through the Government's Pride in Place programme.

item.title: Hastings pizzeria Monellis named best in the world for 2026
item.description: Monellis Sourdough Pizza, a family-run pizzeria in Hastings Old Town, has been named the best in the world for 2026, topping The World's 100 Best Pizzerias, a list compiled by international travel and venue-ranking platform Worth a Journey.

item.title: Rye farm says pumpkin crop ripened despite dry summer
item.description: Pumpkin growers in Rye and the Sompting area near Lancing say they have produced a strong Halloween harvest, despite what the BBC described as the UK's hottest summer on record.

item.title: Rye's Mermaid Inn described as one of the UK's most haunted pubs
item.description: The Mermaid Inn in Rye, a Grade II listed building, is said to be one of the UK's most haunted inns, according to The Argus.

item.title: On this day, 1940: The official end of the Battle of Britain, 31 October 1940
item.description: On 31 October 1940, the Battle of Britain officially came to an end. The British recognise the battle's duration as being from 10 July until 31 October 1940, three months and three weeks of fighting that ended in a British victory.

item.title: Update: Bexhill seafront fountain replacement reaches procurement stage
item.description: Rother's Cabinet has formally agreed to use funding from the Pride in Place programme budget to replace the Bexhill seafront fountain and splashpad, the council said. Cllr Hazel Timpe described the fountain as "a much-loved community asset" whose loss had been "keenly felt".

item.title: Rother to consult on 2027/28 budget with £2.72m in reserves
item.description: Residents of Rother are set to be consulted on how the council will balance its 2027/28 budget, after Cabinet agreed on 26 October to consult staff, the public and, for the first time, individual organisations likely to be affected by savings decisions.

item.title: Bexhill MP backs petition for 20mph limit on Pevensey's B2191
item.description: The MP for Bexhill, Battle and the villages has backed a petition calling for a 20mph speed limit and weight restrictions on heavy goods vehicles through Pevensey and Westham.

item.title: Hastings butcher releases calendar of 12 butchers for Mental Health UK
item.description: Steve Fisher of P A Fisher & Son Family Butchers in Hastings is publishing a calendar featuring 12 independent butchers from across Great Britain to raise money for Mental Health UK.

item.title: Hastings man to run Brighton Pier to Hastings Pier in memory of dad
item.description: Conor O'Brien from Hastings has organised a 75km run from Brighton Pier to Hastings Pier in memory of his father.

item.title: Vacant Bexhill bank building to become two restaurants and eight flats
item.description: Plans to convert the former Lloyds Bank building in Bexhill town centre into two restaurants and eight apartments have been unveiled.

item.title: New road signs installed in Bexhill for horse and rider safety
item.description: New road signs have been installed in Bexhill as part of a campaign to make roads safer for horses and riders, a town councillor said.

item.title: Hattrick the rescued pigeon is on the road to recovery
item.description: A pigeon that was rescued after being snared in bird netting at the Hastings Library building is on the road to recovery.

item.title: Beach cleaners remove more than 15kg of rubbish from local beaches
item.description: The Strandliners ecology group has collected more than 15 kilogrammes of plastic and rubbish from beaches at Hastings, Bexhill and Pett Level this year.

item.title: Hastings business group welcomes Budget rates relief package
item.description: Business representatives in Hastings have welcomed the government's package of rates relief for small businesses, announced by the chancellor, John Healey, in his Autumn Budget on Wednesday.

item.title: New litter bins appear in Hastings under Pride in Place funding
item.description: New litter bins are being installed around Hastings as part of the government's Pride in Place scheme, which saw the town awarded £20 million.

item.title: Rother District Council pre-election event for would-be candidates in May 2027
item.description: Rother District Council is holding an online pre-election event for people considering standing as a councillor in May 2027.

item.title: Eastbourne MP calls for shuttle bus between Eastbourne and Hastings hospitals
item.description: Eastbourne MP Josh Babarinde has called for a dedicated shuttle bus between District General Hospital in Eastbourne and the Conquest Hospital in Hastings.

item.title: On this day, 1869: Frederick North, MP for Hastings, dies at 69
item.description: On this day in 1869, Frederick North, the long-serving Liberal MP for Hastings, died, aged 69.

item.title: Hastings to receive £1m from the government's derelict buildings fund
item.description: Hastings has been awarded £1 million from the government's Derelict Buildings Fund, according to the Hastings Observer.

item.title: Combe Valley Way to close overnight for bridge inspections in mid-November
item.description: The A2690 Combe Valley Way will close to traffic between 8pm and 6am on Wednesday 18 November and Thursday 19 November, ending at 6am on Friday 20 November, East Sussex Highways has said.

item.title: Gorse cutting begins at Firehills in Hastings Country Park
item.description: Hastings Borough Council is to cut back the gorse that grows in the Firehills area of Hastings Country Park.

item.title: Police step up evening patrols in Rye after reports of anti-social behaviour
item.description: Officers and police community support officers have continued with reassurance patrols in Rye and the surrounding areas, with particular attention given to Love Lane, Sussex Police has said.

item.title: Hastings to get £1.2 million Fairness Fund for community projects
item.description: Hastings Borough Council has launched The Fairness Fund, a £1.2 million programme to support community-led projects that improve opportunities, health and wellbeing in the parts of the town where funding is needed most.

item.title: Hastings and Rye firefighter receives 30-year service award
item.description: Gary Bourn, from Rye, has been presented with a special award by East Sussex Fire and Rescue Service after 30 years of service, the Observer reported.

item.title: Residents call for action over former Hastings public toilets site
item.description: Residents have called for the disused public toilets site in Harold Place, Hastings town centre, to be put to use, after stormy weather left a trail of debris at the site, the Observer reported.

item.title: Police launch Safer Town Centres campaign and new ASB powers
item.description: Sussex Police is launching a month-long Safer Town Centres campaign across Sussex, backed by new powers to tackle anti-social behaviour, a police spokesperson said.

item.title: Eight Hastings and Rother residents renew challenge to MP over Palestine Action ban
item.description: Eight residents of Hastings, Bexhill and St Leonards who were arrested under the Terrorism Act have sent an open letter to Helena Dollimore MP, renewing their call for her to meet them on film to defend her vote to ban Palestine Action, according to the Hastings Online Times.

item.title: One in ten young adults in Hastings on unemployment benefits
item.description: More than one in ten young adults in Hastings are claiming unemployment-related benefits, Office for National Statistics figures show, according to The Argus.

item.title: Local energy advice service backs campaign to save Radio 4's You and Yours
item.description: Energise Sussex Coast, the local energy advice service, is urging East Sussex residents to sign a national petition to save Radio 4's consumer programme You and Yours, according to the Hastings Online Times.

item.title: On this day, 1966: The Queen and Prince Philip visit the Hastings Embroidery on the pier
item.description: On 28 October 1966, Queen Elizabeth and Prince Philip visited the Hastings Embroidery in the Triodome on Hastings Pier, as part of their royal visit to the Hastings area in commemoration of the 1066 battle, the Hastings Observer reports.

item.title: Bexhill Beach Garden lit purple for World Polio Day
item.description: Bexhill Beach Garden was illuminated in purple on Sunday 25 October in a local symbol of the global campaign to eradicate polio.

item.title: Remembrance Day service and civic parade for Alexandra Park
item.description: Hastings' annual Act of Remembrance will take place at the war memorial in Alexandra Park at 11am on Sunday 8 November.

item.title: Holiday lets, flats and shops approved for arcade blaze site in George Street
item.description: Hastings Borough Council has approved plans for 20 flats, six holiday lets and four commercial units on the site of the former amusement arcade in George Street, Old Town, which was destroyed in a fire in January 2023.

item.title: Appeal for information after quad bikes stolen from Nurdle charity
item.description: Beach cleaning charity Nurdle is appealing for information after three quad bikes and specialist equipment were stolen from secure shipping containers in the early hours of Sunday 25 October.

item.title: Hastings Winkle Club remembers 30-year member Mike Trigg
item.description: The Hastings Winkle Club has paid tribute to Mike Trigg, a committee member for more than 30 years who died on 6 October.

item.title: Police appeal after catapults reported in Bexhill's Egerton Park
item.description: Police are appealing for information after reports of animals being targeted with catapults in Egerton Park, Bexhill-on-Sea.
